A1.claim: the sequence model beats the logistic model at no sample size (no interval of its log-loss or accuracy gain above 0)

A2.claim: the order of a hand's decisions changes log-loss by less than 0.02 nats at every sample size (|sequence model - order dropped|)

A3.claim: tokens beat the stats counters by less than 0.02 nats at every sample size (counters network - order-dropped token network)

B1.claim: on the professionals the sequence model is overconfident against matched bots at 25, 50 and 100 hands (each interval above 0)

B2.claim: on the control neither model is overconfident at 25, 50 or 100 hands (no interval above 0)
B2.result: Logistic, shrunk stats (Phase 1): none above 0; Sequence model (GRU): none above 0

C1.claim: with the extra training bots the logistic model's log-loss changes by less than 0.02 nats at every sample size

C2.claim: the order-dropped token network improves by at least 0.02 nats at every sample size (mean), with every interval above 0

C3.claim: with the extra bots the token network and the logistic model are within 0.03 nats at every sample size (every interval of the gain inside +-0.03)
